timeline.current_model: ABCA1 is an ATP-hydrolyzing integral membrane transporter that extracts phospholipids from the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane and flips them through a hydrophobic gateway/annulus tunnel into extracellular apoA-I, simultaneously generating lipid domains on the cell surface to which apoA-I binds (directly to ABCA1 at ~10% capacity and to lipid microdomains at ~90% capacity), enabling solubilization of cholesterol and phospholipids into nascent discoidal HDL particles; its activity is regulated transcriptionally by LXR/RXR, RAR, PPAR, AMPK-LXRα, HIF-1β, and multiple repressors (OSBP, ORP8, TRAK2, p62/mTOR), post-translationally by calpain-mediated degradation (destabilized by unsaturated fatty acid–activated PLD2 phosphorylation, AGE-RAGE-ubiquitin/lysosome pathways, and OSBP), and by endosomal recycling (clathrin/Rab5 endocytosis; Rab4/ARF6-regulated return to plasma membrane); beyond cholesterol efflux, ABCA1 suppresses TLR4-driven macrophage inflammation through membrane lipid raft remodeling, activates JAK2/STAT3, PKA, PKC, and CDC42 signaling upon apoA-I binding, controls beta-cell cholesterol homeostasis and insulin secretion, regulates hepatic VLDL secretion, modulates aqueous humor outflow via a caveolin-1/eNOS/NO pathway, maintains brain apoE lipidation and neuroinflammatory tone in an astrocyte-specific manner, and exerts tumor-suppressor function in myeloid cells by restraining IL-3Rβ/MAPK/JAK2 signaling.
